data.raw_text:
Weeks of flooding near Manila have left Filipinos furious — not just at the rains, but at decades of alleged corruption. Despite ₱545B ($9.6B) spent on flood-control projects in just 3 years, many works exist only “on paper”, President Marcos Jr admitted.

Resignations have followed, contractors face probes, and the lavish lifestyles of political “nepo babies” flaunting private jets and designer outfits online have become lightning rods for public rage.

Protests are planned as citizens demand transparency, accountability, and real flood protection.
